title: Impact of Welfare Eligibility on Labor Supply
research_question: How does eligibility for welfare benefits, determined by an income threshold, affect individuals' labor supply? Specifically, does crossing the income threshold for welfare eligibility lead to a reduction in hours worked?
data_description: The dataset includes 500 observations with columns: running_var (income), treated (indicator for eligibility), and y (hours worked). The data focuses on individuals near the income threshold for welfare eligibility to assess its impact on labor supply.

ground_truth.identification_strategy: Examine changes in labor supply around the income threshold for welfare eligibility.
ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the income threshold for welfare eligibility results in a reduction in labor supply.

_fix_notes.description: Ground-truth effect and direction corrected to match actual data. Root cause: extend_exp_b_to_100.py:267 applied abs() before passing effect to make_rdd(), so the synthetic CSV has positive effect while the JSON recorded the original signed value. Data file unchanged; only JSON metadata updated.
